prompt:
Scene:
A straight-on studio catalog photograph of a medieval-scale triptych altarpiece, centered in the frame, softly lit from above as if in a museum case. Dark velvet backdrop, crisp edges, no depth distortion.

Subject:
A three-panel altarpiece with gothic pointed-arch tops. The central panel is taller; the two side panels are hinged open. Each panel's surface is a grid of small colored glass cells separated by dark lead bead lines, each cell clearly backed by a glowing LED pixel. The glass cells form a pictorial field of clustered geometric saints rendered in a bead-style mosaic; the central panel shows a symmetric haloed figure in robe, the two side panels show donor-like attendants. A copper-circuit moulding runs around every panel edge, with tiny soldered nodes.

Important details:
Each glass cell must feel thick and slightly uneven, with a visible bead line between cells. The LED backing behind each cell must be a clean, discrete pixel — you should read both the glass thickness and the pixel through it. Copper circuit moulding must look real: oxidised patina, hand-laid traces, small solder dots. Color palette: deep indigo cell fields, gold and ruby accents, warm copper frame, cool white LED backing. Keep the three panels identically proportioned.

Use case:
Reference image for a fanout series. Later images must preserve the exact triptych frame, glass-cell grid density, copper moulding pattern and panel symmetry.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no gospel verses printed, no brand corporate saints, no modern HDMI ports visible, no church donor name plaques, no people in front of the altar.
title: Reference Altar
description: Master reference establishing the LED-backed triptych altarpiece with colored-glass cells, copper circuit moulding and a symmetric central saint.
